title: evening-rubric-scrapbook-anika-shah
body:
Evening scratchpad — ad-hoc rubric + odd outputs (wfh, late notes)

Context / goal:
- Quick capture of what I tried tonight while investigating a weird regression on streaming token order for the quantized 3B variant.
- Not a finished doc; this is my working mental model + sample outputs + lightweight scorecard to crystallize next steps.

Why this matters:
- Customers (small-mid SaaS) hit occasional token reordering when using short prefix caching + quantized models under burst. We need reproducible steps and an ad-hoc rubric to triage severity quickly.

Ad-hoc rubric (quick scoring: 0–3, 0=no issue, 3=critical):
1) Output coherence (0–3): Are tokens semantically jumbled? -> 2 (often sentences ok, occasional mid-sentence swap)
2) Prompt fidelity (0–3): Does model follow instruction? -> 1 (mostly yes)
3) Regeneration stability (0–3): Do repeated decodes vary widely? -> 2 (high variance with same seed + cache reuse)
4) Latency impact (0–3): Does fix/behavior change latency >10%? -> 1 (small but measurable on 8 token prefixes)
5) Safety/regulatory surface (0–3): Does this cause hallucinated claims that would block enterprise customers? -> 0 (not yet)

Quick notes on experiments run (timestamps local):
- 2025-01-12 20:05 — baseline: float16 3B, no prefix cache, single request. No reordering observed.
- 2025-01-12 20:22 — quantized int8+KV cache enabled, same prompt, 1/5 runs had token swap at ~step 46.
- 2025-01-12 20:45 — raised beam size (n=1 still) but disabled prefix caching: no swap.
- 2025-01-12 21:10 — re-enabled cache with shorter prefix (8 tok): swap frequency increased to 3/10.
- 2025-01-12 21:40 — attempted replay with same RNG seed + identical KV: swap reproduced 2/3 times => suggests non-determinism in cache eviction codepath or kernel scheduling on GPU.

Representative sample outputs (raw, verbatim)
- Prompt: "Summarize the meeting about Q1 rollout in three bullets."
  Baseline (float16): "- Prioritize infra automation. - Freeze minor feature toggles by Feb. - Coordinate with sales for pilot."
  Quantized+cache (affected run): "- Prioritize infra automation. - Freeze minor by feature toggles Feb. - Coordinate with sales for pilot."
  
  Notes: second bullet has token order swap "minor by feature toggles Feb" — not catastrophic but user-facing flaky text.

Oddities noticed:
- Swap tends to move small function words and adjacent tokens (prepositions, determiners) rather than core content words.
- More likely when response length > 40 tokens and prefix cache size is between 6–12 tokens.
- Doesn't appear when running on a different kernel (tried alt-kernel-3). Could be scheduling vs memory alignment.

Initial hypothesis chain:
1) Quantized kernel introduces misaligned memory access when merging KV cache slices => occasionally writes overlap, producing swapped token emission order.
2) Async GPU scheduling + our prefix trimming routine may race with the kernel's incremental KV updates.
3) Less likely: beam/decoding randomness; more evidence points to deterministic write/read interleaving under high throughput.

Tests to validate (short-term):
- Add deterministic barrier after KV merge and run 100 replayed seeds. Metric: swap_count. (JIRA: JIRA-IR-489)
- Force using alt-kernel-3 across quantized path to see if incidence drops to zero.
- Add byte-level diff of KV buffers before/after merge to detect partial writes (heavy but decisive).

Customer exposure and severity assessment:
- Severity: low→medium for now (non-malicious, mostly phrasing oddities). But could degrade user trust if frequent.
- Impacted stack: customers using dedicated+quantized variants with prefix caching and bursts. Likely hit smaller models (3B) most.

Short TODO (priority order):
- [ ] Create a minimal reproducer script (python) that toggles cache size and runs 100 deterministic seeds. Tie to CI job. (owned: me)
- [ ] Instrument KV merge with a cheap checksum (XOR) before/after writes. (owned: Carlos)
- [ ] Post quick note to #serving-runtime with sample outputs + link to PR. Mentioned in slack thread (see linked_artifacts). (owned: me)
- [ ] Draft short customer blurb if incidence reaches >0.5% in production. (low priority)

Ideas for longer-term fixes / mitigations:
- Ingest small prefix cache fallback: when reordering detected, automatically reroute to float16 variant for that session. (Ops policy config)
- Offer a "safe quantized" flag that enforces kernel compatibility checks at startup.
- Improve our rollout monitors: add a quick histogram of token-level edit distance vs baseline for real-time alerts.

Notes to self (random):
- Keep notebook with raw KV buffer dumps compressed (store offline due to size).
- Check PR #1387 re: atomic writes in KV merge code — looks relevant (linked above).
- Follow up with Priya about whether optimize suggestions could flag this pattern (quality evasion when prefix caching enabled).

Unresolved questions:
- Is this purely GPU kernel bug or something in our serialization of KV slices?
- Are any enterprise customers already seeing this at scale and not surfacing it? (ask CS)

Bottom line (for tonight): I have a reproducible-ish pattern tied to quantized + prefix cache. Next step: write reproducer + quick checksum instrumentation. If that shows deterministic corruption, escalate to kernel vendor with a small minimal repro and a KV snapshot.

-- end of scratchpad --

Timestamp of last run: 2025-02-20 22:34 local
Coffee status: cold but effective.
